mainTopic: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's rulings after the חורבן on חדש and on accepting witnesses for the new month, and the mistake the לויים made in the שיר
overview: The amud opens by explaining why רבן יוחנן בן זכאי forbade new grain (חדש) for the whole sixteenth of ניסן after the חורבן. He followed רבי יהודה, who reads 'עד עצם היום הזה' as 'until and including that day,' so the prohibition is from the Torah. The גמרא deals with a משנה where רבי יהודה seems to argue with him. It answers that רבי יהודה misunderstood him, and that 'התקין' there means 'he explained the פסוק and set the practice.' Then a new משנה tells a three-stage history: witnesses for the new month were first accepted all day. After a late arrival made the לויים go wrong in their שיר, they were accepted only until מנחה. After the חורבן, רבן יוחנן בן זכאי brought back the all-day practice. The גמרא asks what the לויים' mistake was. The scholars in בבל say they sang nothing, while רבי זירא says they sang the weekday song. רבי זירא's proof from the word 'שיבוש' is answered. Then רב אחא בר הונא brings a ברייתא about a Thursday ראש השנה. Its words 'says it and repeats it' show that the weekday song was sung while the day was in doubt.

steps.title: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי followed רבי יהודה's reading of the verse
steps.stepSummary: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's ruling that חדש is forbidden all of יום הנף follows רבי יהודה. רבי יהודה reads 'עד עצם היום הזה' as 'until and including that day.'
steps.simpleTranslation: He made this rule following רבי יהודה's view. רבי יהודה says the פסוק 'until this very day' means until the day itself, and that 'until' includes the day. So without the עומר, new grain is forbidden by the Torah for the whole sixteenth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from the previous section: why did רבן יוחנן בן זכאי forbid new grain for the entire day? The answer is that he held like רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without the עומר, the only thing that permits חדש is the day itself. רבי יהודה holds 'עד' is inclusive ('עד ועד בכלל'), so the whole sixteenth is still forbidden. That makes the ruling a Torah prohibition, not just a rabbinic safeguard.

keyTerms.meaning: the day itself, the 'essence' of the day
the day of waving the עומר, the sixteenth of ניסן

steps.confusionAlert: 'עד ועד בכלל' does not mean the grain becomes allowed when the sixteenth begins. It means the sixteenth itself is still included in the prohibition.

phrases.english: He said it following the approach of Rabbi Yehuda,
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבן יוחנן בן זכאי, and 'it' is his rule that new grain is forbidden all of the waving day.

phrases.english: who said: "Until this very day"
means until the day itself.
And he holds: "until" means until and including.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from the previous section about why the whole יום הנף is forbidden.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributes the ruling to a specific תנא's reading of the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ruling seemed to be only a rabbinic safeguard.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ruling follows רבי יהודה, under whom the whole day is forbidden by the Torah.

steps.title: A משנה shows רבי יהודה disagreeing with רבן יוחנן בן זכאי
steps.stepSummary: How can רבן יוחנן בן זכאי follow רבי יהודה? A משנה shows רבי יהודה objecting to his ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does he really hold like רבי יהודה? רבי יהודה disagrees with him! A משנה says: after the Temple was destroyed, רבן יוחנן בן זכאי instituted that the whole waving day is forbidden. רבי יהודה said: 'But isn't it already forbidden by the Torah, as the פסוק says, until this very day?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from step 1. It quotes a משנה where רבי יהודה seems to argue with רבן יוחנן בן זכאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי יהודה protests 'isn't it already forbidden by the Torah?', he must think רבן יוחנן בן זכאי meant something different. So they look like they disagree. That clashes with the claim that רבן יוחנן בן זכאי followed רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: But does he hold like him?
But he clearly disagrees with him,
as we learned in a mishnah:
After the Temple was destroyed,
Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai instituted
that the entire day of waving be forbidden.
phrases.notes: Forbidden to eat new grain, that is.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said:
But isn't it forbidden by the Torah,
as it is written: "Until this very day"!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי סָבַר לַהּ כְּווֹתֵיהּ? וְהָא מְפַלֵּיג פְּלִיג עֲלֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks step 1's claim that רבן יוחנן בן זכאי follows רבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's ruling follows רבי יהודה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the משנה, רבי יהודה protests against רבן יוחנן בן זכאי, which shows they disagree. So רבן יוחנן בן זכאי cannot be following him.

steps.title: רבי יהודה misunderstood רבן יוחנן בן זכאי
steps.stepSummary: There is no real disagreement. רבי יהודה thought the rule was rabbinic, but רבן יוחנן בן זכאי meant it was a Torah law.
steps.simpleTranslation: In that משנה, it was רבי יהודה who made a mistake. He thought רבן יוחנן בן זכאי was making a rabbinic rule. That is not so: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי was teaching a Torah law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by saying the argument in the משנה was only a misunderstanding.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's protest assumed the rule was a rabbinic addition. In fact רבן יוחנן בן זכאי agreed it was a Torah law. So the two agree about the law itself, and step 1 stands.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the prohibition on new grain for the entire sixteenth, when there is no עומר, is a Torah law. It is not just a rabbinic safeguard.

phrases.aramaic: הָתָם — רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הוּא דְּקָא טָעֵי.
phrases.english: There, it was Rabbi Yehuda who erred.
He thought

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי מִדְּרַבָּנַן קָאָמַר,
phrases.english: Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai was speaking of a rabbinic law,
but that is not so;
he was speaking of a Torah law.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם — רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הוּא דְּקָא טָעֵי
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets the dispute as a misunderstanding
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה and רבן יוחנן בן זכאי really disagree.
steps.terutzMaskana: They agree. רבן יוחנן בן זכאי meant a Torah prohibition, and רבי יהודה misread him as making a rabbinic one.

steps.title: But the משנה says he 'instituted'
steps.stepSummary: The משנה uses the word 'התקין' (instituted), which sounds like a rabbinic rule, not a Torah law.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the משנה says 'he instituted'! That word means making a new rabbinic rule.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on step 3. The wording of the משנה itself seems to show the rule was rabbinic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A תקנה is normally something the חכמים add on their own. If the משנה calls it 'התקין', it sounds rabbinic. That would mean רבי יהודה understood it correctly after all.

phrases.english: But it teaches "instituted"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 3's claim that the rule was from the Torah.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבן יוחנן בן זכאי meant a Torah law
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word 'התקין' describes a rabbinic enactment. That fits better with the rule being rabbinic.

steps.title: 'Instituted' means he explained the verse and set the practice
steps.stepSummary: 'התקין' here means he explained the פסוק and set up the practice based on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'instituted' mean? He explained the פסוק, and based on that he set the practice.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by explaining what 'התקין' means here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי did not create a new rabbinic law. He taught people the Torah's rule from the פסוק and set it as the practice from then on. So the word 'התקין' fits a Torah-level rule too.

keyTerms.meaning: he explained the פסוק and set the practice

steps.whatToRemember: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's rule follows רבי יהודה. Without the עומר, new grain is forbidden by the Torah for the entire sixteenth of ניסן. רבי יהודה's objection in the משנה was a misunderstanding. 'התקין' means 'explained the פסוק and set the practice.'

phrases.english: What does "instituted" mean?
He explained the verse and set the practice.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 4's challenge from the wording.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'התקין' means he explained the פסוק and set the practice, so the rule is from the Torah.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The prohibition on new grain for all of יום הנף, when there is no עומר, is from the Torah, following רבי יהודה's reading. רבן יוחנן בן זכאי taught it publicly after the חורבן.

steps.title: Originally, witnesses were accepted all day
steps.stepSummary: The משנה opens by saying that at first, בית דין accepted testimony about the new moon at any time during the whole day.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: At first, they used to accept testimony about the new month all day long.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It tells us the original practice: witnesses who saw the new moon could come and testify at any point on that day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the starting point of a short history. The words 'at first' tell us the practice will soon change. The rest of the משנה explains why it changed and how it was later restored.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה; the text the גמרא will discuss
Testimony from witnesses who saw the new moon, used to set the start of the month

phrases.english: MISHNA:
At first, they would accept
testimony about the new month the entire day.
phrases.notes: This is about the thirtieth day of אלול. If witnesses came that day, it became ראש השנה.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּרִאשׁוֹנָה הָיוּ מְקַבְּלִין עֵדוּת הַחֹדֶשׁ כׇּל הַיּוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. It moves on from the earlier discussion of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's rule about חדש on יום הנף.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Originally, עדות החודש was accepted throughout the entire thirtieth day.

steps.title: A late arrival leads to a new cutoff at מנחה
steps.stepSummary: One year the witnesses came late and the לויים sang the wrong song. Because of this, the חכמים ruled that witnesses would be accepted only until מנחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once the witnesses were delayed in coming, and the לויים got the song wrong. So they instituted that testimony would be accepted only until מנחה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה tells the story that caused the rule to change. Because witnesses showed up late one year, the חכמים set a deadline of מנחה time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the בית המקדש the לויים sang a set שיר each day, and a יום טוב needed a different one. Late in the day nobody knew yet whether it was יום טוב, so the שיר came out wrong. A cutoff at מנחה meant everyone knew in time which day it was.

keyTerms.meaning: They were delayed; they took a long time
Things went wrong for them; they made a mistake
The לויים in their daily song in the בית המקדש
They instituted; they made a new rule

phrases.english: Once, the witnesses were delayed in coming,
and the Levites went wrong in the song.
phrases.notes: They didn't yet know if the day was ראש השנה, so they weren't sure which שיר to sing.

phrases.english: They instituted that they would not accept testimony
except until מנחה time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the original all-day practice from step 6 was changed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After the incident with the לויים, testimony was accepted only until מנחה.

steps.title: Witnesses after מנחה: keep both days holy
steps.stepSummary: If witnesses came after מנחה, people still treated that day as קודש, and they also treated the next day as קודש.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if witnesses came from מנחה time and later, they would treat that day as holy, and the next day as holy too.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now explains what happened under the new rule when witnesses arrived too late. People kept that day as קודש anyway, and the next day was also קודש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Testimony that came after the deadline was not used to set the date, so the next day became the official ראש השנה. But the day the witnesses came was still kept holy. That way people would not get used to treating that day as a regular weekday.

keyTerms.meaning: From מנחה time onward; after the cutoff
They treat it as; they act as if

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the day the witnesses came was the official ראש השנה. It was only treated as קודש. The next day was the real ראש השנה, and the dates of the coming months were counted from it.

phrases.english: And if witnesses came
from מנחה time and onward,
they would treat that day as holy,
and the next day as holy.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם בָּאוּ עֵדִים מִן הַמִּנְחָה וּלְמַעְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Works out what the new מנחה cutoff from step 7 means when witnesses come late.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Witnesses who came after מנחה did not set the date, but both that day and the next were kept as קודש.

steps.title: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי restores the all-day practice
steps.stepSummary: After the בית המקדש was destroyed, רבן יוחנן בן זכאי ruled that testimony about the new month would again be accepted all day.
steps.simpleTranslation: After the בית המקדש was destroyed, רבן יוחנן בן זכאי instituted that they would accept testimony about the new month all day.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends by saying that after the חורבן, רבן יוחנן בן זכאי went back to the original practice of accepting witnesses all day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מנחה cutoff existed because of the לויים and their שיר in the בית המקדש. Once there was no בית המקדש, that reason was gone. So the old practice from step 6 came back.

keyTerms.meaning: From when the בית המקדש was destroyed
He instituted; he set up a rule

steps.whatToRemember: There are three stages. First, witnesses were accepted all day. Then, after the mix-up with the לויים, only until מנחה. After the חורבן, רבן יוחנן בן זכאי brought back all day.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is one more example of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי making new rules after the חורבן. It shows how a rule can end once the reason behind it is gone.

phrases.english: After the Temple was destroyed,
Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai instituted
that they would accept testimony about the new month
the entire day.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשֶּׁחָרַב בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ הִתְקִין רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the history begun in step 6 by cancelling the cutoff from step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After the חורבן, עדות החודש is again accepted the entire day.

steps.title: What did the לויים get wrong in the שיר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what exactly the mistake of the לויים in the שיר was.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: What mistake did the לויים make in the song?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by asking about a detail of the משנה: what went wrong with the לויים' song. This question sets up the two answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said the לויים 'messed up' the שיר when the עדים came late, but it did not say how. The גמרא wants to know what the mistake actually was.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
The Levites, who sang in the בית המקדש
The song sung during the קרבנות

phrases.english: GEMARA
What mistake did they make,
the Levites, in the song?
phrases.notes: This goes back to the משנה in Step 7, where the עדים came late and the לויים sang wrong.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the details of the song mistake mentioned in the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What exactly the לויים did wrong in the שיר

steps.title: The view in בבל: they sang no song at all
steps.stepSummary: The scholars in בבל explain that the לויים did not sing any song at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here in בבל they explained: they did not say any song at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The scholars in בבל give the first answer: the לויים did not sing anything.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the day's status was still unclear at the afternoon תמיד, the לויים did not know which song to sing. So, according to this view, they stayed silent.

phrases.english: Here they explained:
phrases.notes: 'Here' means בבל, where this גמרא is being learned.

phrases.english: that they did not say a song at all.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The mistake was that no song was sung at all

steps.title: רבי זירא: they sang the weekday song
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא says the לויים sang the regular weekday song with the afternoon תמיד, instead of the יום טוב song.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: they sang the weekday song with the afternoon תמיד.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא gives a different answer: the לויים did sing, but they sang the wrong song.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי זירא's view, the mistake was doing the wrong thing, not doing nothing. When the עדים came later, it turned out the day was ראש השנה, so the weekday song was wrong.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
that they said the weekday song
with the afternoon daily offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second, competing answer to the same question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The mistake was singing the weekday song instead of the יום טוב song

steps.title: רבי זירא sends a ברייתא to בבל
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא tells his son אהבה to teach a ברייתא saying the rule was made so the song would be sung 'without a mistake'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said to his son אהבה: Go out and teach them: They instituted that testimony about the month would be accepted only if there was enough time left in the day to offer the תמידין, the מוספין and their נסכים, and to sing the song without a mistake.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא brings a ברייתא to support his view against the scholars in בבל. This step sets up the argument in the next step, which turns on the word 'שיבוש'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the תקנה was made so the song would be sung 'without שיבוש'. רבי זירא will argue that this word fits his explanation better.

keyTerms.meaning: The extra קרבנות of the day

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי זֵירָא לְאַהֲבָה בְּרֵיהּ,
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said to Ahava his son,
go out and teach them:
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the scholars in בבל who said the לויים sang nothing.

phrases.english: They instituted that they would not accept
testimony about the month unless
there would be enough time in the day
to offer the daily offerings, the additional offerings and their libations,
and to say the song without a mistake.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי זֵירָא לְאַהֲבָה בְּרֵיהּ פּוֹק תְּנִי לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי זירא brings a source to back his own answer
steps.raayaObject: רבי זירא's view that the לויים sang the wrong song
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that uses the word 'שיבוש' for the song mistake

steps.title: The word 'mistake' fits only a wrong song
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא argues that 'שיבוש' means doing something wrong, which fits singing the wrong song but not singing nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works if you say they sang the weekday song, because then there is a mistake. But if you say they did not sing at all, what mistake is there?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא spells out his proof: the word 'שיבוש' shows that the לויים did something wrong, not that they did nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Singing the wrong song is clearly a 'mistake'. Staying silent seems like leaving something out, not a mistake. So the word in the ברייתא seems to challenge the view in בבל.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well if you say

phrases.english: Granted, if you say
they said the weekday song,
that is where there is a mistake.
But if you say
they did not say a song at all,
what mistake is there!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the ברייתא in Step 13
steps.kashyaTarget: The view in בבל that no song was sung at all
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'שיבוש' means a wrong action, and silence is not an action

steps.title: Silence is the biggest mistake of all
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that not singing at all is also a שיבוש, in fact the greatest one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since they did not sing at all, there is no greater mistake than that.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the view in בבל: leaving out the song entirely counts as a mistake too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא read 'שיבוש' as only a wrong action. The answer is that the word also covers leaving out the song completely, which ruins the עבודה even more. So the ברייתא fits both views.
steps.whatToRemember: The word 'שיבוש' in רבי זירא's ברייתא fits both views: no song at all (בבל) or the weekday song (רבי זירא). The view in בבל survives this proof, but steps 16–19 bring a new challenge against it from a ברייתא quoted by רב אחא בר הונא.

phrases.english: Since they did not say a song at all,
you have no mistake greater than this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the word 'שיבוש'
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'שיבוש' means only doing the wrong thing
steps.terutzMaskana: Leaving out the song completely is the greatest שיבוש

steps.title: רב אחא בר הונא quotes the songs of ראש השנה
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר הונא starts an objection by quoting a ברייתא listing the songs for the morning תמיד, the מוסף, and the afternoon תמיד on ראש השנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר הונא objected: The morning תמיד of ראש השנה is offered in its usual way. At מוסף, what does one say? 'Sing aloud to God our strength, shout to the God of Jacob.' At מנחה, what does one say? 'The voice of ה׳ shakes the wilderness.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר הונא opens a challenge by quoting a ברייתא. This step only sets up the source; the actual point of the objection comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the morning תמיד gets its normal weekday song, while מוסף and the afternoon תמיד get special ראש השנה songs. This list of songs will be used to challenge the view in בבל that the לויים sang nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: The extra קרבן of the day
The afternoon time and its תמיד

phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Huna raised an objection:
The daily offering of Rosh Hashanah in the morning
is offered according to its usual rules,
phrases.notes: He means the לויים sing the regular song for that day of the week.

phrases.english: At the additional offering, what does one say?
"Sing aloud to God our strength,
shout to the God of Jacob."
At the afternoon offering, what does one say?
"The voice of the Lord shakes the wilderness."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new challenge to the explanations of the song mistake
steps.kashyaTarget: The view in בבל (step 11) that when the day is in doubt, the לויים sing no song at all
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup: quotes the ברייתא's list of ראש השנה songs. Its Thursday clause (steps 17-18) will show that, in a doubt, the weekday song was sung. That works against the view in בבל.

steps.title: On a Thursday ראש השנה, the morning song is changed to avoid repeating
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: when ראש השנה falls on Thursday, "הרנינו" is not said in the morning, because it will be said at מוסף. Instead they say the section starting "הסירותי".
steps.simpleTranslation: And when ראש השנה falls on a Thursday, whose regular song is "Sing aloud to God our strength," one would not say "Sing aloud" in the morning, because then he would go back and repeat that section. So what does he say instead? "I removed his shoulder from the burden."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is still quoting רב אחא בר הונא's ברייתא, which explains a special Thursday case. This is setup for the objection that comes in step 19.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The normal Thursday song is מזמור פא in תהלים, which begins "הרנינו". On ראש השנה that same song is also used at מוסף. To avoid singing the same section twice in one day, the morning תמיד gets the later part of that מזמור, starting from "הסירותי".

keyTerms.meaning: On Thursday (the fifth day of the week)
"Sing aloud to God our strength", the opening of מזמור פא and the regular Thursday song
Goes back and repeats the same section
"I removed his shoulder from the burden", a later verse in the same מזמור

phrases.english: And when ראש השנה falls
to be on Thursday,
whose regular song is
"Sing aloud to God our strength":
one would not say "Sing aloud" in the morning,
because he would go back and repeat the section.
phrases.notes: "הרנינו" is also the ראש השנה מוסף song in the ברייתא's list, so singing it in the morning would mean singing it twice.

phrases.english: Rather, what does he say?
"I removed his shoulder from the burden."

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבִזְמַן שֶׁחָל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה לִהְיוֹת בַּחֲמִישִׁי בַּשַּׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא quoted by רב אחא בר הונא in step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that when the day is in doubt, no song is sung at all
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup only: it establishes that on Thursday the morning song is changed so it won't be repeated.

steps.title: If the witnesses came late, the song is repeated anyway
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends: if the עדים came after the morning תמיד, they say "הרנינו" at מוסף even though it repeats the section.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the witnesses came after the morning תמיד, he says "Sing aloud", even though he goes back and repeats the section.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last line of the ברייתא, and it is the key line the objection will be built on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the עדים came late, then in the morning nobody yet knew it was ראש השנה. The ברייתא says that "הרנינו" is then said at מוסף 'even though it repeats'. That means it was already said once that morning, while the day was still in doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: Witnesses who saw the new moon, whose testimony makes the day ראש השנה

steps.confusionAlert: Don't miss the hidden point: the ברייתא never says outright what was sung in the morning. The words 'even though it repeats' only make sense if "הרנינו" was already sung in the morning, as the normal Thursday song.

phrases.english: And if the witnesses came
after the morning תמיד,
he says "Sing aloud"
phrases.notes: He means at the מוסף, once they know it is ראש השנה.

phrases.english: even though he goes back
and repeats the section.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם בָּאוּ עֵדִים אַחַר תָּמִיד שֶׁל שַׁחַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the exception to step 17's rule: when the עדים come late, the repetition is allowed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that when the day is in doubt, no song is sung at all
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup: the phrase 'repeats the section' suggests the weekday song was sung while the day was still in doubt.

steps.title: The repetition proves the weekday song is sung when in doubt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the objection. 'Repeats it' makes sense if, in a doubt, we sing the weekday song. If no song is sung in a doubt, what was repeated?
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well if you say that whenever there is a doubt we sing the weekday song. That is why the ברייתא says he says it and repeats it. But if you say no song was sung at all, what does 'he says it and repeats it' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now spells out רב אחא בר הונא's challenge from the ברייתא. It works only if, in a doubt, they sang the regular weekday song.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On a doubtful Thursday morning, singing the weekday song means singing "הרנינו". Singing it again at מוסף really is a repeat. If in a doubt they sang nothing, "הרנינו" would be sung only once, so the ברייתא's words 'repeats it' would make no sense.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well if you say...
Where there is a doubt (whether today is ראש השנה)

steps.whatToRemember: From the Thursday case: when the day was still in doubt, the לויים sang the regular weekday song. That is the only way "הרנינו" could end up being 'repeated'.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא gives clear support for רבי זירא's position from step 12 that the weekday song was sung, and it pushes against the idea that they stayed silent.

phrases.english: It works well if you say
that anywhere there is a doubt
we sing the weekday song,
that is why it says:
he says it and repeats it.
But if you say
they did not sing at all,
what does "he says it and repeats it" mean?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא כׇּל הֵיכָא דְּמִסְתַּפְּקָא אָמְרִינַן שִׁירָה דְחוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the inference from the ברייתא's words 'repeats the section' in step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that when the day is in doubt, the לויים sing no song at all
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A repetition requires that "הרנינו" was already sung in the morning while the day was in doubt. That only happens if the weekday song is sung in a doubt. So the 'no song' view cannot explain the ברייתא.
